svg.title: How the cost of an order is measured
svg.desc: The order-cost test uses fleet fights, three ships a side, all six of one hull: fighter, strafer or gunship. Two match panels show three azure darts on the left, labelled pilots being tested, and three ember darts on the right, labelled free side. In Run 1: ordered, each ship is ordered to attack the enemy nearest it, chosen again every 2 s. Its pilot sees the order. Each azure dart has an order line with an open arrowhead pointing toward the enemy nearest it, which is ringed in azure. A down arrow leads to Run 2 beside the note: The same matches again: same starts, same line-ups, same pilots. Run 2: no orders shows the same ships in exactly the same places within its panel, without order lines or target rings. The same pilots get no orders at all. They fight on their own judgment. The free side, in both runs, is the same opponent in both runs, flying free. Its own commander gives orders, but they are hidden from its pilots, so they fight on their own judgment. Below that panel's heading, an ember box labelled its commander sends a dashed ember order line toward an ember dart. The line stops at a short wall bar labelled hidden before reaching the ship. The cost is calculated as Order cost = win rate in run 1 minus win rate in run 2, compared match by match, 1,152 matches in each run. Below zero: the order loses fights. Near zero: the order is cheap to follow. Win rate: the share of matches won, out of 1, a draw counting half.
